snapshot.plan_label: GE 4,603, the eve of Blàr Àth na Fala (ERA_PLAN); the same year is FE 1 in the count that opens at the king's fall
snapshot.description: Ailean Mòr has been king of the godkin for four thousand six hundred and two years. He holds the hill of Dùn ìseal in his own hand again, as in the first days, for the list of those who held it under him ended with Catrìona Mhòr; the Red Hill on the lake keeps its own holders and is sworn to him and not to the hill; the salt shore, the north and the west have set their hands in his at the great gathering at the ford. At Tobar dhìreach nine keepers drawn by lot watch the slab, and the king does not overrule them. Every hearth of the hills burns its handful by the one stone measure, the sharing before the storms is kept on every coast, and the saying is spoken at every gathering, but none of it is declared and no oath is yet sworn over the vein. The Old Ones have been silent for four thousand years and their harbours are empty but for Seann Skell and a few that the hill-folk have taken up. East of the vein the households who never bowed have gathered their spears at Dùn dhearg and are coming down to the ford below it, while the king's kin wait in tents in the valley under Dùn ìseal for their shares.

land_changes.what: The oak has fallen back from the northern lowlands (GE 3,588): heather, birch and bog-moss as on the master map, groves only in the sheltered valleys.
Loch chrom stands a hand higher on the Ros dhomhain tide-rock than at the first cut; no change to the drawn shore.
The lake dwellings of Loch chrom are burned (GE 1,525); the charred piles stand in the shallows.
The crack across the valley at Cill ghlas, banked with stones and marked by a line of white stones.

new_burgs.name_en: the heirs' camp in the valley under Dùn ìseal
new_burgs.role: the king's kin come in from every coast to wait for their shares: a fire and a steward for each line, more than any reciter can name in a night
new_burgs.reason: the kin wait about the king for their shares at the snapshot; they stay on after the Binding to part the kingdom

new_burgs.name_en: the war-camp of the eastern host
new_burgs.role: the spears of the east, gathered since GE 4,520, moving down to the ford below Dùn dhearg
new_burgs.reason: the host that comes against the king at the ford (FE 1); its numbers are not told, only that its dead dammed the river

new_burgs.name_en: the salt-folk's shelters at the ford gathering
new_burgs.role: the ford where salt was first traded for wool: salt people downstream, hill people upstream, flint people on the far bank, Dùn dhearg on ground of its own
new_burgs.reason: the yearly gathering at the ford from GE 1,208; no one is said to live there between gatherings (Muileann òg is founded in the Holy Age)

new_burgs.name_en: the ring of shelters at the warm springs
new_burgs.role: pilgrims in numbers; the eldest healing-tale is set here
new_burgs.reason: a ring of shelters built GE 2,455; the bath-house comes only in FE 529

ruler.title: Rìgh Chlann nan Dè
ruler.note: crowned in the grove GE 1 aged 24; about 4,626 years old; has held Dùn ìseal in his own hand since Catrìona Mhòr died (GE 4,391)

ruler.note: the Stone Kings' list does not name the holders of Dùn dhearg

polities.name: Luchd-faire na Lice
polities.form: nine keepers drawn by lot, one for each district of the hills; they hold no land but the slab and the keepers' house, and the king does not overrule them

ruler.note: nine keepers by lot; they meet at the slab only when a keeper dies. The first keeper by lot was Oighrig nic Dhòmhnaill (GE 2,403).

admin_units.name_en: the nine districts of the hills (one keeper each)
admin_units.kind: lot districts, not bounded on any record

diplomacy.note: Uisdean Mòr knelt to the king on the lake shore; the Red Hill swears to the king and not to Dùn ìseal, so neither list names the other until the peace of the ford.
The king bade the east come in; they sent his messenger back with nothing and gathered their spears at Dùn dhearg. The host comes to the ford at the snapshot.

diplomacy.relation: separate charges: the king rules the grazing and the gatherings, the slab rules the vein
diplomacy.note: Calum Ciar was refused the lot; Catrìona Mhòr neither refused nor granted the keepers' asking to be named. The matter is left to the next age.

diplomacy.relation: none recorded; the handful is burned in the hills alike

cultures.name: Na Dia-thìrich
cultures.note: The hill-folk take the names Dia-thìrich and Dia-thìr in this age (by GE 2,201), and with them the belief that they did not come. They order themselves by blood and recite seven names back before a marriage.

cultures.name: Na Seann-Dhaoine
cultures.note: No work of theirs is dated after the half-cut stone of GE 510; by GE 551 they are silent. They hold no land at the snapshot; their names stay on the harbours with Seann before them.

faiths.name: An Seann Urram
faiths.name_en: the old reverence of the hearths
faiths.form: hearth reverence with a custody of the vein by lot
faiths.practice: The measured handful in the stone cup, burned on one dark night of the year; the nine keepers of the slab by lot; the sharing of surplus before the storms; the saying spoken at every gathering; the unlit hearth; the dead rowed to Eilean ìseal on the south-east coast. It is one reverence: nothing is declared and no god is named at the hearth.

faiths.name: Aithris a' Chruthachaidh
faiths.deity: Caoran and the Tuath Dè, who crowned Ailean in the grove
faiths.practice: Kept by the Children of the Question with the Line of the Mason and, apart from it, the Line of Somhairle. Ailean tells no one what the gods put into him.

routes.rule: A master trail or sea-lane is present when every town it touches stands in this age (or both its end towns stand and at most a quarter of the sites between are not yet towns); trails and lanes that touch no town, and the roads and lanes the annals date later, are absent. The two great carrying ways of the age are added.

new.name_en: the flint road
new.note: worn by the flint-carriers from Cnoc àrsaidh south and east toward the ford gathering; near Àth leathan their feet sink it a yard deep

new.name_en: the salt road
new.note: from the pans of Baile ghorm by the ford gathering to the north-west; at Muileann àrsaidh salt costs three times its price at the pans

new.name_en: the stepping-stones of the Abhainn fhionn
new.note: the first made crossing of any river on the island

new.name_en: the road of the salt and wool (the Red Hill to the ford)
new.note: Murchadh Gearr walked the salt road every year to be seen on it; Dùn chrom's bank faces both ways between the Red Hill and the hills of the vein

master.note: Pilgrims in numbers and a ring of shelters; a herder came lame and walked home. The herds of Dùn ìseal wintered here under Gormshuil and drank here in the dry year.

master.era_name_en: the beacon on the north-western headland
master.note: The headland fire of Baile chrom, one of the five points the coasts are lit at.

master.era_name_en: the storm beacon on the eastern cape
master.note: Kept by the coast households in turn to bring boats home in a storm, not to warn them off.

master.era_name_en: the shore-fire on the northern point
master.note: Its ash goes down through three yards of fire-reddened soil.

master.era_name_en: the fire on the north-eastern cape
master.note: Steps cut up to it from the shore, narrower than those at Seann Bhral.

master.era_name_en: the fire on the southern cape
master.note: Kept for the boats of the south coast; with the other four the coasts are lit at five points.
The western shaft of the Old Ones; stones thrown in are not heard to land.
A youth was let down on a rope of plaited hide to the rope's end and drawn up alive; he never told what lay below, and no one goes down again in this age.
Four watchers on the Seann Skell tower see a back as long as three boats; wreckage of stitched boats washes up in the western water.
A herding family that lit an open fire vanished; two herders without a fire saw a figure walk the ridge breathless, and lived. The covered hearth spreads to Muileann chiar.

master.era_name_en: the uncut forest of the white stag
master.note: Pilgrims sit a night at the line of the trees without entering; their small fires lie all along the edge.
A child of Cnoc bheag went past the line of stones and was not found; the settlers take timber only from the far side of the river.
The obelisk with the unread line and the four Dia-thìris words.
Cuimhnich an teine, in its ring of fire-cracked stones.

After Anndra Breac was put out of the ford for saying "we came", the saying on the column is spoken as a rule at the opening of the gathering; its worn words are recut by a hand from the hill (GE 4,364).
Ruin of the Old Ones' outpost; the households of Cathair mhòr below take no stone from it.
Ruin of the fortress; the fishers of Ceann mhin will not go up to it.
The temple ruin: the Dia-thìrich pass it without stopping, and a path is worn round it at a distance.

master.era_name_en: the cairns of the heads of households on the hill
master.note: A cairn for each head of a household at death, on the slope above the cattle-fold; some forty by the end of the age.
The gathering at the eight wind-stones of Ceann leathan ends with wrestling and the lifting of stones; the black boulder lies there still.

Raghnall Ceannfhionn and the holder of the Red Hill agreed salt for wool here; it became the yearly gathering. At the great gathering (GE 3,000) the holders set their hands in the king's with four hundred of his blood about him. Both king-lists were recited here whole.
A boat hollowed from one oak trunk, long enough for six, sunk and left at the landing.
The panthers turn back at the foothills (a hard winter follows); cattle driven into the passes out of season are taken.
A family by the burial ground takes on the clearing of thorn; diggers break into a grave lined in the Old Ones' manner, close it and move the row.
The keeper's cup and its three copies set side by side on a flat stone and filled from the spring in turn.
The Mason's Point.

new.name_en: the crowning in the grove
new.note: Ailean kept the seven fires seven nights, fasting; on the eighth Caoran came with the Tuath Dè and named him Rìgh Chlann nan Dè, and put into him the power that was in the coals.

new.name: Àth na Fala
new.name_en: the ford below Dùn dhearg (named for the blood after the battle)
new.note: The ford where the host of the east comes against the king. The battle opens the next day: he holds it alone three days and three nights, the dead of the host dam the river, and he falls on the third night. The ford is called Àth na Fala after.

new.name_en: the boundary stones of Dòmhnall Clachach
new.note: Marker stones along the valley below the hill, parting the grazing of Dùn ìseal from its neighbours'; some still stand and are argued over.

new.name_en: where the Red Hill knelt
new.note: Uisdean Mòr came down to the lake shore and knelt to the king.

new.name_en: the shingle of Baile ghorm
new.note: Iain Dubh, the king's son, was slain here raiding the salt; the king came down alone, and none struck. The salt shore became his without blood.

new.name_en: the keepers' house and the stone cup
new.note: A house for the holder of the lot, its door facing the slab; Oighrig nic Dhòmhnaill's cup of grey stone, the measure of every handful; the coal of Gilleasbuig Beag laid back under the slab.

new.name_en: the hawk lintel of Àth mhòr
new.note: A hawk carved over a house door, wings closed, head turned: the oldest carving of any bird on the island.

new.name_en: the wolf graves of Tobar fhiadhaich
new.note: Wolves buried whole and with care, laid on their sides as people are.

new.name_en: Gilleasbuig Beag's island
new.note: The keeper who took coal was rowed out to Eilean chrom and left without a boat; his fire was seen three nights. The island stays empty and unfished.

new.name_en: the tide-rock of Ros dhomhain
new.note: High-water marks cut at an even interval on a boulder in the harbour mouth; Seònaid Mhòr cut hers in pairs. A third rock is kept at Inis thais.

new.name_en: the stone of the Black Wind
new.note: A stone set in the midst of Ceann chiar with a mark for every house the Black Wind took: twenty-two.

new.name_en: the white stones of the fault
new.note: A line of white stones along the crack; no house within a stone's throw. Broken in two places when the ground shook again, and laid again.

new.name_en: the first trench for another vein
new.note: Diggers from Dùn ìseal opened it seeking coal like the vein's and left it when two were crushed. A second opening elsewhere found common rock, and the prospecting ended.

new.name_en: the tally wall of Seann Warr
new.note: The Old Ones' counting stones built into a wall, some three thousand strokes; they thicken together in the bad years.

new.name_en: the half-cut stone
new.note: The last tally stone of the Old Ones, two strokes finished and a third begun and forsaken.

new.name_en: the wind-stones and the eight notches
new.note: The eight wind-names cut on the high point of Eilean fhada as on the main island; eight tall stones on the point at Ceann leathan.

new.name_en: Eilean ìseal, the island of the dead
new.note: The households of the south-east coast begin to row their dead here after the old manner of the Old Ones.

new.name_en: the long-house of Cathair gheal
new.note: Forty paces long, byre and hall under one roof; twice burned and twice rebuilt on the same footing.

new.name_en: the wind-stone of Seann Chwen
new.note: A wind-name cut in the Dia-thìreach manner over an older mark of the Old Ones.

zones.name_en: the first kingdom: the hill and its valleys (GE 1)
zones.note: Ailean takes the hill and brings the households of the valleys under his hand.

zones.name_en: the Red Hill bends the knee (GE 290)
zones.note: The Red Hill keeps its holders and swears to the king.

zones.name_en: the salt shore bends the knee (GE 728)
zones.note: No blood is shed and none is paid.

zones.name_en: the great gathering at the ford (GE 3,000): the north and the west set their hands in the king's
zones.note: Only the households east of the vein send no one.
Pots left full of boiled bark and seaweed; the grave-rows doubled. The oldest hunger tied to a place.
The springs run dry so long that the field banks are forsaken; the fields are cut anew on another line.

zones.name_en: the ground opens at Cill ghlas (GE 827; again GE 3,863)
zones.note: A crack a man could fall into; a spring moves a hundred paces downhill and back.

zones.name_en: the waves at Cnoc chaol (GE 777; GE 3,817)
zones.note: Sand a hand thick with deep-water shells over the hearths; the second wave takes no house.

zones.name: A' Ghaoth Dhubh
zones.name_en: A' Ghaoth Dhubh, the Black Wind (GE 2,417)
zones.note: Strips the thatch from every house of the east coast from Cuan ruadh to Ceann chiar; the coast feeds Cuan ruadh through the winter from its shared surplus.

zones.name_en: the host of the east (GE 4,520 to the snapshot)
zones.note: The households east of the vein, sworn to owe nothing to Dùn ìseal, gather their spears at Dùn dhearg.

zones.name_en: the last counts of the Old Ones (GE 308–551)
zones.note: Strokes on midden stones, the tally wall of Seann Warr, the count at Seann Tarr; the bad years on three coasts at once; the half-cut stone; silence.
The oak falls back; heather, birch and bog-moss spread over the northern lowlands and the winters lengthen.

labels.text_en: the kin wait for their shares

labels.text: Cha do thàinig sinn; bha sinn ann
labels.text_en: we did not come; we were here

hosts.name_en: the host of Dùn dhearg and the eastern households
hosts.strength: not told; its dead dammed the river
hosts.note: Gathered at Dùn dhearg since GE 4,520; at the snapshot it comes down to the ford.

hosts.name: Ailean Mòr
hosts.note: He holds the ford alone three days and three nights; the kin who should have come are quarrelling over the shares.

hosts.name: Ìomhar Dearg
hosts.note: A son of the king, some fourteen hundred years old; still in the valley arguing for river-grazing. He rides east late, falls on the spent host the morning after the king falls and takes Dùn dhearg.

sides: the salt-pans that did not own the king
campaigns.note: The first war in either list; seven fell on the hill side.

campaigns.name_en: the death of Iain Dubh and the king at Baile ghorm
campaigns.note: Iain Dubh slain on the shingle; the king came alone and the salt shore knelt.

campaigns.name_en: the king's wars over the island
campaigns.note: The lists keep no count of the wars the king rode to, only that he came home from all of them but the last. How he won, none who stood against him could say.

campaigns.name: Blàr Àth na Fala
campaigns.name_en: the Battle of the Ford of Blood (opens the next day)
sides: the host of Dùn dhearg and the east
campaigns.note: Shown as imminent: it is the opening event of the Holy Age.

arms.note: No arms: the first arms on the island are the seal of the vein-house in the Age of Sundering.

arms.signs: the red stone of the hill (inferred)
the stone cup of grey stone
arms.note: No arms; the cup is the keepers' measure and token.

polities.rioghachd: The first kingdom is one man: Ailean Mòr, crowned by the gods in the grove, who took the hill of Dùn ìseal and brought the island under his hand in four and a half thousand years of riding. His children and kin held the hill for him one after another and are counted as the Stone Kings; since the last of them he has held it himself. He has told no one what is in him.
polities.red-hill: The Red Hill on the lake is an old line not of the king's blood, which knelt to him and kept its own holders and its own list. It traded salt for wool with the hill at the ford and fostered a son of Eilidh Ghlas. Its list ends with Seumas Òg, and its name is not yet Cathair dhearg.
polities.dun-dhearg: East of the vein the households raised a double-banked fort at Dùn dhearg and never came to the gatherings until Catrìona Mhòr's time, and then only to trade. When the king bade them come in they swore to owe nothing to him. Their host is at the ford.
polities.keepers: The keepers of the slab are drawn by lot, one for each of the nine districts of the hills, and watch the burnt vein at Tobar dhìreach. They refused Calum Ciar the lot, and the king would not overrule them. They have asked to have their charge declared before the whole gathering, and it has not been.

burgs.315: Dùn ìseal: two banks and ditches on the hill the first king took, the shared store within them, the valley below full of the tents of his kin.
burgs.19: The Red Hill: ditch and palisade across the neck of the hill above the lake, a laid-stone landing at the river-mouth, and the Red Hill list kept by its reciters.
burgs.422: Dùn dhearg: a double bank on the grass plateau east of the vein, where the spears of the east have gathered.
burgs.276: Tobar dhìreach: the slab, the keepers' house facing it, the lot of the nine and the pilgrims; Clann na Ceiste keep the lines here.
burgs.27: Ros dhomhain: some sixty houses round the tide-rock, the greatest place on the shores of Loch chrom.
burgs.489: Seann Skell: hill-folk families in the Old Ones' river harbour, using the old mole and mending none of it.

province_polity_notes.rioghachd: The bounds of the five holdings are not recorded; they are drawn from the places each holding's settlers came from and went to. Dùn thais (16) is set in the north: at the parting after the king's fall it lay on the line between the north and the east.
province_polity_notes.dun-dhearg: East of the vein: every province whose households sent no one to the gathering. The Holy Age reads Dùn thais and Achadh mhòr as border ground.
province_polity_notes.unclaimed: Only the island shires without people and the windy coast (no province) are left; the king's holdings are taken to reach every settled coast west of the vein.
